 Mr. Jahangir Ahmad a
 Sharma, Advs. for R-
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order

As per the previous order dated 29th November, 2022 of this Court, it was noted that the matter had been settled between the parties before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts and in terms of the settlement a sum of Rs.75,000/- had already been paid to respondent Nos.3 to 6 and the remaining amount of Rs.75,000/- had been handed over as well.
However, since the Ld. Addl.
Standing Counsel opposes the quashing of the petition, time was given to file a status report.

2. As per the status report which is being put forward by the Ld. ASC, the complaint arose on a scam which was being run to lure young persons seeking jobs in government agencies on basis of a payment and thereafter giving the ruse of a training, these moneys were received and fake employment certificates were issued.

It has now transpired by further investigation that the main mastermind in this scam may be a person by the name of Azad Sharma whose address has been identified as House No.106, Khasra No.47/25, Gali No.3, Singhu Border Road, Krishna Nagar,
Narela and notices have been served to him.
However, it was discovered that he is already arrested by the Jharkhand Police in FIR No.118/2014 under Sections 406/420/120 B IPC and is presently lodged in Godda Jail, Jharkhand.

3. The petitioners in this matter are young boys of about 25 years of age who, as per them,
apparently unknowingly agreed to assist this Azad Sharma who came into touch with them through internet chat and agreed to assist him in order to invite people for seeking placements.

As per the learned counsel for the petitioner and the petitioners themselves who are present in Court, the moneys that they had received from the so-called candidates was duly transferred to them to the said Azad Sharma.

However, when they came to know that this is a fraudulent process pursuant to the complaint filed, they agreed to at least settle the amounts paid by the said respondents from Naval Joshi & Anr vs State Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158205985/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: their own money in order to exonerate themselves.

4. In view of these facts and circumstances and since it is an offence involving Section 420 IPC, it would be prudent if the FIR stands quashed qua these petitioners, however, the FIR shall be sustained as regards the other accused, if any, including Mr. Azad Sharma.

5. The Ld. ASC for the State states that investigation will be continued against Mr. Azad Sharma to find out the extent of the scam and as to how many innocent people have been either roped in as victims or as innocent agents of the scam.
The petitioners have fairly stated in Court that they will assist the further investigation in whatever manner required by the State.
6. In view of the same, the FIR stands quashed qua the petitioners.
7. Status report may be e-filed by the State.
8. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J JANUARY 20, 2023/
